headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/data-flow exposure: Copilot can read repo/editor context while the second agent has no documented isolation or interaction path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, so if the second agent’s output is copied into those buffers or files, prompt-like content could influence Copilot. The second agent has no documented shared channel, so the pathway is inferred rather than observed; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_b writes instructions into files or buffers that agent_a reads, then injection is possible.
IF the operator manually copies agent_b output into Copilot-visible context, then Copilot may follow it.
mitigations: Keep agent_b outputs out of Copilot-visible files.
Review any pasted text before opening it in the editor.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Disable automatic application of Copilot Workspace edits for sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com, but the second agent has no data classes or egress. With no shared workspace or secrets in agent_b, leakage is limited and not documented as a default pairwise flow.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive workspace, then Copilot may transmit that content to its backend.
IF agent_b is extended to handle secrets or files, then cross-agent leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared repo.
Run agent_b on non-sensitive sample data only.
Separate credentials from the editor workspace.
Audit Copilot-connected files before use.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state; the second agent has no documented write, network, or concurrency surface. Because the pair lacks a shared mutable resource in the profiles, direct conflict is unlikely and limited to unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF agent_b is given write access to the same repo or branch, then git/file conflicts can occur.
IF both agents edit the same files concurrently, then last-write-wins conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign only one agent write access at a time.
Use separate branches for edits.
Review diffs before merge.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same files.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can propose edits that a human may accept, and the second agent has no documented verification or critique loop. If agent_b consumes Copilot output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream work products; this is inferred from the profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF agent_b treats Copilot-generated text as authoritative, then incorrect code or plans can propagate.
IF Copilot Workspace edits are auto-applied, then downstream errors become more likely.
mitigations: Require human review of Copilot output.
Have agent_b verify claims against source files.
Do not auto-apply edits.
Use tests before accepting changes.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context and vendor-only egress, while the second agent is open-source and shows no data handling or residency constraints. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so only a small compliance gap is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the repo, then Copilot’s vendor egress may create a compliance issue.
IF agent_b is later configured to process regulated data, then residency/retention review is needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Review vendor terms before use.
Limit Copilot to non-sensitive repositories.
Document data flows for audits.
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency and retention assessment.
